stories.headline: Bridging the Gap Between Scripture and Theology
stories.summary: Kevin Vanhoozer is navigating the intersection of biblical studies and theology in a post-'demise of biblical civilization' world. His work aims to provide a framework for interpreting God's Word in a rapidly changing landscape.

stories.headline: AI Transparency: A Promise Unfulfilled
stories.summary: Anthropic's support page claims to explain how they plan to implement transparency in AI-generated content, but critics argue it falls short of providing concrete details. The company's commitment to transparency remains unclear.

stories.headline: iOS 27 Beta 5: New Features and Tweaks
stories.summary: The latest iOS beta introduces several new features, including tweaked app icons and improved Siri voices. Users can now adjust the pace and expressivity of Siri's voice to suit their preferences.

stories.headline: Boosting LLM Inference on Apple Silicon
stories.summary: A recent discovery has revealed that Apple Silicon and macOS VMs can achieve 11-16 times faster LLM inference with the use of Llama.cpp. This breakthrough has significant implications for AI developers and researchers.

stories.headline: Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs
stories.summary: A new article has exposed the vulnerability of proprietary LLM APIs, highlighting the risks of stealing reasoning traces from these systems. This raises concerns about the security and integrity of AI models.

stories.headline: Praying Through Pain with Constant Devotion
stories.summary: Glenna Marshall's book 'Praying in Pain' offers guidance on how Christians can cultivate a spirit of prayer and devotion, even in the midst of chronic health conditions. Her approach emphasizes the importance of perseverance and faith.

stories.headline: Russia Uses North Korean Missiles to Strike Ukraine
stories.summary: Ukraine's president has accused Russia of using ballistic missiles from North Korea to carry out strikes in Zaporizhzhia, resulting in the deaths of seven people. The incident highlights the ongoing conflict in the region.

stories.headline: Houthis Launch Deadly Attack on Small Cargo Ship
stories.summary: The Houthi rebels have reportedly carried out a deadly attack on a small cargo ship, killing four people in the process. The incident marks a significant escalation of tensions in the region.

stories.headline: Turkey Offers Conditional Pardon to PKK Militants
stories.summary: Turkey's parliament has approved legislation that would introduce a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants, in an effort to advance the government's peace initiative with the insurgent group. The move aims to bring an end to the conflict.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Risky Business Model
stories.summary: Nvidia is expanding its business model to allow customers to raise money, but this move significantly increases the risk of the AI buildout. The company's strategy has sparked concerns about the stability of the AI industry.

stories.headline: Apple Brings Live Baseball to Vision Pro with Immersive Experience
stories.summary: Apple's 'Friday Night Baseball' will now be broadcast live in 3D on Vision Pro, offering an immersive experience for baseball fans. The 8K video will provide a 180-degree field of view, putting viewers right in the action.

stories.headline: GitHub Copilot Hacked Behind a Proxy, What Was Learned
stories.summary: A developer put GitHub Copilot behind a man-in-the-middle proxy to learn more about its inner workings and how it generates code suggestions. The experiment provided valuable insights into the AI-powered coding tool.

stories.headline: AI-Driven Web Changes Erase Internet's Collective Memory
stories.summary: As AI-powered tools increasingly dominate the web, the internet's collective memory is disappearing, threatening the preservation of historical information and cultural heritage. Google search is just one example of this trend, where relevant results are becoming harder to find.

stories.headline: Churches Mobilize to Support Local Schools with Community Service
stories.summary: A church initiative aims to build trust with local schools by providing support and care for students' needs, fostering a sense of community and cooperation between the two institutions. By doing so, schools can refer students to the church for help, strengthening their partnership.

stories.headline: Chuck Timely & The Hourglass: A Time-Traveling Session Musician's Debut
stories.summary: Songwriter Tucker Pillsbury has reinvented himself as a time-traveling session musician, releasing a country record that's more nostalgic than innovative. While charming, the album's ersatz barroom country sound may not convince all listeners.

stories.headline: Meta Unveils Muse Glimmer, a New 30B Model with Apache 2.0 License
stories.summary: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30B model under the Apache 2.0 license, marking a significant improvement over previous licenses. The model is optimized for local tasks, such as end-to-end agent interactions, and promises to be a powerful tool for developers.

stories.headline: Go Language Ideal for AI-Assisted Software Engineering
stories.summary: Google has identified Go as an ideal language for AI-assisted software engineering due to its simplicity, concurrency features, and garbage collection. These characteristics make Go an attractive choice for developers working with AI-powered tools and frameworks.

stories.headline: Bashar al-Assad Sentenced to Death for War Crimes and Crimes Against Humanity
stories.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former President Bashar al-Assad to death in absentia for committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war. The verdict marks a significant development in the pursuit of justice for victims of the conflict.

stories.headline: Assad Sentenced to Death for Crimes Against Humanity and War Crimes
stories.summary: A Syrian court has sentenced former President Bashar al-Assad and his brother to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes committed during the country's 14-year conflict. The verdict highlights the ongoing efforts to hold perpetrators accountable for their actions.

stories.headline: Thailand Introduces Tough New Laws After Mass Shooting
stories.summary: Thailand has suspended new gun permits and promised tough new laws in response to a mass shooting, which has highlighted the country's high levels of firearms ownership. The move aims to reduce gun violence and improve public safety.

stories.headline: Native MiniMax-H3 Inference Lands on Apple Silicon
stories.summary: A new open-source project brings native MiniMax-H3 inference to Apple Silicon, promising faster and more efficient performance for AI applications. This development could have significant implications for the growing ecosystem of AI-powered devices.

stories.headline: Mountain Goats' Latest Album Is a Hilarious and Polished Ride
stories.summary: The Mountain Goats' new album is a masterclass in storytelling, with the band's performances conveying the same nuance and range as John Darnielle's writing. The result is a hilarious and polished ride that's sure to delight fans of the band.

stories.headline: National Guard Marks One Year in D.C., Colombia Hit by Deadly Quake
stories.summary: Today marks one year since the National Guard was deployed to the nation's capital, and the impact is still being felt. Meanwhile, a devastating 7.4 magnitude earthquake has left over 100 people dead in Colombia.

stories.headline: British Singer-Songwriter Tackles Personal Upheaval with Dry Wit
stories.summary: On her third album of elaborate art-pop, the British singer-songwriter tackles personal upheaval with dry wit, unconventional production, and a more cohesive vision. The result is a compelling and thought-provoking listen.

stories.headline: Midwest Rock Group Channels Regret and Reckoning on New Album
stories.summary: The Midwest rock group's sixth album is a moodily introspective work that balances post-hardcore propulsion with disarming buoyancy. The result is a compelling and emotionally resonant listen.

stories.headline: Lebanon Abolishes Death Penalty in Landmark Vote
stories.summary: Lebanon's parliament has voted to abolish the death penalty, making it the first country in the Middle East to end capital punishment. The new law still needs cabinet approval before it can take effect.

stories.headline: Voters Head to Polls, Trump Signals Shift on Iran
stories.summary: Voters in six states head to the polls today for high-profile primaries, while Trump signals a shift in his strategy with Iran. Meanwhile, a devastating 7.4 magnitude earthquake has left over 100 people dead in Colombia.

stories.headline: Libyan Oil Refinery Hit by Drone Strike in Third Incident
stories.summary: Libyan authorities are battling a major blaze at the Zawiya oil refinery, which was hit by a drone strike for the third time in two days. The incident highlights the ongoing instability in the region.

stories.headline: France to Ban Unsolicited Telemarketing Calls
stories.summary: France is set to ban unsolicited telemarketing calls from today, in a move aimed at protecting consumers from unwanted sales pitches. The ban is part of a broader effort to regulate the use of personal data.

stories.headline: Interactive Website Lets You Scroll Through 43 Quintillion Rubik's Cube States
stories.summary: A new interactive website lets users scroll through all 43 quintillion possible states of a Rubik's Cube, providing a unique and mind-bending experience. The website is a testament to the ingenuity of its creator.

stories.headline: OT Laws Get a Strange New Twist
stories.summary: A recent trend of biblical law interpretations has some questioning the boundaries between faith and modern society. Critics argue that these interpretations are being used to justify discriminatory practices.

stories.headline: Trump's Secret Plane Swap Exposed
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump allegedly used a ruse to avoid reporters, hiding in a catering truck while switching planes over an Iran threat. The incident has sparked controversy and raised questions about presidential transparency.

stories.headline: New Git Tool Simplifies Commit Messages
stories.summary: A new GitHub tool, Git-knife, allows users to edit commit messages, authors, and dates in a spreadsheet-like interface. This could streamline the development process and improve collaboration among team members.

stories.headline: US Marine Released from Russian Custody
stories.summary: Former US Marine Robert Gilman, who was arrested in 2022, has been released from Russian custody on a humanitarian basis. The move comes after reports of his poor health and catatonic-like state.

stories.headline: Midwife Bridges Maternity Care Gap
stories.summary: A Black midwife in Alabama is working to address the shortage of labor and delivery hospitals in rural areas, providing critical care to mothers and babies in need. Her efforts highlight the importance of accessible healthcare for marginalized communities.

stories.headline: Colombia Devastated by Massive Earthquake
stories.summary: A powerful earthquake has struck Colombia, leaving at least 169 people dead and a state of emergency declared. The disaster has caused widespread destruction and displacement, with rescue efforts underway.

stories.headline: New App Generates Video Courses on Any Topic
stories.summary: Keet, a mobile app, allows users to create video courses on any subject, with short videos and games for reinforcement. The app aims to make learning more engaging and accessible.

stories.headline: Alabama Primary Election Marred by Confusion
stories.summary: The second primary election in Alabama has been plagued by confusion and concerns about low voter turnout, following the state's redrawing of congressional maps. The situation has raised questions about the effectiveness of the electoral process.

stories.headline: Progressive Candidates Face Tests in Midwest Primaries
stories.summary: Competitive primaries in Minnesota and Wisconsin will test the power of progressive candidates, with questions about their ability to win in November and the GOP's chances of picking up moderates. The outcome could have significant implications for the 2024 elections.

stories.headline: Manus Returns to Independent Status
stories.summary: Manus, a company, has announced that it will be returning to its independent status after a period of uncertainty. The move has sparked interest among users and investors, with questions about the company's future plans.

stories.headline: England on Track to Eradicate Hepatitis C
stories.summary: England is poised to become one of the first countries to eliminate hepatitis C, thanks to a concerted effort by health officials and medical professionals. The achievement is a significant milestone in the fight against the disease, which has long plagued global health.

stories.headline: Chicken Scheme 6.0 Released
stories.summary: The latest version of the Chicken Scheme programming language has been released, featuring a range of improvements and new features. Developers can now take advantage of the updated language to build more efficient and effective applications.

stories.headline: Philippines River Choked with Rubbish
stories.summary: Heavy rainfall has left a trail of destruction in its wake, with a river in Manila overwhelmed by a tide of trash and debris. Cleanup efforts are underway, but the scale of the problem remains a significant challenge.

stories.headline: Wildfires Devastate Spokane Neighborhoods
stories.summary: Aerial footage captures the devastating aftermath of a series of wildfires that swept through Spokane, leaving homes and cars reduced to rubble. The full extent of the damage is only now becoming clear.

stories.headline: Woman Pulled Over Twice Due to Flock Camera Glitch
stories.summary: A woman was pulled over at gunpoint not once, but twice, after a Flock camera incorrectly identified her vehicle as a suspect. The incident highlights the potential risks of relying on AI-powered surveillance systems.

stories.headline: Astrology App Store Rejection Story Retracted
stories.summary: A prominent tech blogger has retracted a story about an astrology app being rejected from the App Store, citing concerns about the accuracy of the information. The retraction is a setback for efforts to reform the App Review process.

stories.headline: LA Schools Introduce Limited Screen Time
stories.summary: Educators in the Los Angeles school district are preparing for a new policy that limits classroom screen time, a move that some teachers say will be a difficult adjustment. The policy aims to promote healthier learning habits and reduce distractions.

stories.headline: France Bans Unsolicited Telemarketing Calls
stories.summary: France has introduced a ban on cold calling, a move that consumer groups are hailing as a "small revolution" in the fight against unwanted sales pitches. The ban is expected to improve the lives of millions of French citizens.

stories.headline: Luigi Mangione Appears in Court Ahead of Murder Trial
stories.summary: Luigi Mangione has appeared in court as questions continue to surround the case ahead of his murder trial. Prosecutors and Mangione's lawyers are engaged in a battle over evidence, with the trial expected to be a highly publicized event.

stories.headline: The SpaceX Sham Exposed
stories.summary: A new article has shed light on the business practices of SpaceX, revealing a complex web of tax breaks and subsidies that have helped the company achieve its success. The article raises questions about the true cost of SpaceX's ambitions.
